builtBy: Merged on 2026-11-26 from each build's data/<sport>/commits.json (each round as `rounds` records it), by person (data/players.json id). A college two files held is one record, with both files' programs and sources; a commitment two files held (Katarina Smith's, in field hockey and soccer) is one, the better-sourced record with the other's sources added.
notes: Each person's college commitment, in any sport, under the person's registry id (data/players.json): a person has at most one. A build shows the commitments of the people on its varsity rosters this season, found through data/<sport>/player-index.json, so a two-sport player's commitment is on both builds' pages and stays with her from season to season.

The research rules are each round's (`rounds`, README "College commitments"): official sources only, social media only as an official account's post, every commitment checked twice. `pnpm build-players` keeps the file keyed (an id the registry retires is rewritten to the one that stays, `name` to the official name); nothing else in it is ever written by a script.

every candidate re-read by hand (SportsRecruits' commits feed not re-read: HTTP 429). 2026-11-13, the round after the fall signing day (Nov 11), over every varsity row and JV player: the colleges' November signing-class releases (every college in the file, every Division I and II field hockey program, Division I women's lacrosse and West Coast programs in other sports), the lists and the clubs' commitment pages read whole, Stick Together and school, student and local news since Nov 5, every linked SportsRecruits profile re-read and its commits feed for program ids 1 to 1,044; Later rounds, the last on 2026-11-22, are described in the notes. A further round on 2026-11-25 over all four builds (README and DATA-SOURCES §1.15).
notes: Which players on the tracked varsity rosters (the 43 teams of the four leagues swept on 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04, the six Eastern Athletic League teams swept on 2026-10-04, and the 53 Southern California teams swept on 2026-10-06) a public page says have committed to play a sport in college, joined to data/rosters.json on team slug + MaxPreps athleteId. Field hockey is the site's sport, but a commitment in any sport counts (since 2026-10-04): many players here also play lacrosse, soccer or basketball, and commit there. Only players on those rosters are named (varsity rows; rows the overlay marks JV, graduates, and players at schools with no MaxPreps rows are out of scope: six of the 43, Corning, one of the six EAL teams' schools, and eight of the 53 Southern California teams), each under the roster's own spelling.

The linking rule is the one data/clubs.json uses: a public page must name the player and the college in the context of one sport, and either name the player's high school, or give a class year that agrees with the roster grade together with a location in the school's half of the state, Northern or Southern California (the player's hometown, or a club or team based there; "CA" alone is not enough). A nickname or a given name (Samantha for Sami) counts when the page otherwise meets the rule and something beyond the name backs it (a second page, the player's own page naming the same club, or a club she is already tied to in data/clubs.json); such a match is medium unless a page names the school (revised 2026-10-06). A name alone never makes a match, and a class year that disagrees with the roster grade rules one out; two same-name players in one region (two class-of-2027 Phoebe Millers, in Larkspur and San Francisco) are told apart by a page that names the school. College interests, offers, visits, camps, watchlists, a plan to play somewhere ('planning to continue her career at …'), and a place on a college's club team are not commitments.

Social media is a source only as a post by an official account (since 2026-10-12): a college's athletics or team account, the player's high school's, or a club's, cited as an 'official-social' source that names the account and a page that is not social media proving it is the owner's (lib/commits-schema.ts). A player's own post, or any other person's, is never a source (lib/clubs-schema.ts BANNED_HOSTS), only a lead; many commitments are announced only there, so a commitment with no other public page is not in this file. X posts can be read without a login; Instagram, Facebook and TikTok cannot be read from the research environment. Every source names the player or is the player's own recruiting profile; quotes and bases are kept for maintainers and never rendered. A page that draws what it shows only once a script runs (SportsRecruits' /committed/<club> pages and profiles' TEAMS blocks and 'Committed to … on M/D/YYYY' tooltips, MAX Field Hockey's search) may be cited since 2026-11-13 (owner decision), quoting what it shows once rendered, when two separate rendered reads agree; the basis says the quote is from the rendered page. Until then such pages were leads only, and every quote had to be in the page's own HTML. STEPS California's page answers plain requests with a bot challenge but serves its table as HTML, which WebFetch reads.

status: 'signed' only where a source says signed; otherwise 'committed'. No source found by 2026-10-06 said any player had signed. asOf: the earliest date a kept source gives for the commitment (a dated story's own date, or the month a story says the player committed), or null. Every kept source was confirmed by two independent reads. A date that only one read saw is not used: MAX Field Hockey's hidden table dates, and the 'Committed to … on M/D/YYYY' tooltip SportsRecruits draws on a profile with a script.

confidence: high = one first-hand page names the player, the college and the school, or it is the player's own recruiting profile showing the commitment; medium = the match rests on one line of a compiled list plus class year and a club in the school's half of the state.

Not run for these rows: SportsRecruits' athlete search, which turned up every commitment in the file that rests on a SportsRecruits profile; the 17 freshmen and sophomores got no web searches; Lassen County's local news sites refused requests.
